summary.headline: 12 candidate decisions are recorded; 9 candidates remain in the bounded assessment queue.
summary.interpretation: Candidate priority controls analyst attention only. It cannot create, promote, or demote an Operating Model requirement.

selection_policy.commitment_boundary: A reviewer must update the calibrated case record before the Operating Model can change.

candidate_pool.title: Open, local & efficient inference
candidate_pool.description: Open-weight, quantized, on-device, and efficiency-focused approaches that reduce dependence on hosted frontier APIs.

adjudication.decision: Treat open and local inference as an execution option, not a universal standalone requirement.
adjudication.rationale: Open weights, quantization, and local runtimes expand the available inference portfolio. They become operationally relevant when a task needs lower cost, lower latency, data control, offline behavior, or provider independence. Those decisions are already captured by heterogeneous routing and the governed proprietary-data boundary; requiring local inference everywhere would ignore quality, maintenance, and hardware tradeoffs.

evidence_review.finding: Quantized runtime integration, adaptive inference research, and wider open-weight availability strengthen technical feasibility. The corpus still lacks independent production comparisons proving that local execution beats hosted inference after quality, operations, fallback, and hardware costs are included.

candidate_pool.title: Voice & audio interfaces
candidate_pool.description: Speech recognition, synthesis, cloning, audio generation, and real-time voice systems used as human or agent interfaces.

adjudication.decision: Treat voice as a conditional interface and workflow domain, not a general startup operating requirement.
adjudication.rationale: Voice is technically credible and increasingly usable, but adoption depends on the user, environment, latency tolerance, accessibility needs, and workflow economics. Startups that choose voice inherit the existing obligations for verified completion, escalation, consent, fraud resistance, and measurable workflow outcomes; other startups should not add voice merely because the modality is advancing.

evidence_review.finding: Full-duplex models, self-hosted stacks, multilingual systems, and practitioner tooling show strong capability breadth. The corpus does not establish that voice is a default operating layer, and impersonation risk plus domain-specific recognition failures make it unsuitable as a universal requirement.

candidate_pool.title: Proprietary enterprise data is moving behind a governed model boundary
candidate_pool.description: Firms will keep proprietary data in systems they control and expose only permitted context or computation to replaceable models, rather than contributing that data to general model training.

adjudication.decision: Add an experimental requirement for startups handling proprietary, regulated, or customer-confidential data.
adjudication.rationale: The actionable conclusion is not that every company must self-host a model. It is that the company-controlled data layer should remain separate from replaceable models, with explicit controls for scoped access, training use, retention, deletion, human access, execution, audit, and provider exit.

evidence_review.finding: Benchling supplies one detailed tenant-isolation and exfiltration architecture; federated and trusted-computation systems make the pattern technically credible. Provider announcements show demand but do not verify contractual guarantees, while channel-level privacy leakage remains an unresolved counter-signal. The evidence clears experimental, not emerging, maturity.

candidate_pool.title: Small & specialized models
candidate_pool.description: Compact or task-specific models optimized for cost, latency, privacy, or a narrow operational decision.

candidate_pool.title: Coding agents & developer tooling
candidate_pool.description: AI systems that search repositories, write and review code, run tools, validate changes, and participate in software delivery.

adjudication.decision: Treat coding agents as an application domain, not a standalone operating requirement.
adjudication.rationale: Coding agents make release gates and bounded workflow ownership more urgent, but "use coding agents" is not a defensible universal requirement. The reusable operating obligations are verified completion, constrained actions, review, rollback, and measurable workflow outcomes.

evidence_review.finding: Failure and adoption evidence strengthens the case for independent release gates, while frequent overclaiming and weak verification practice prevent bounded workflow ownership from advancing beyond narrative maturity.

candidate_pool.title: Frontier inference infrastructure
candidate_pool.description: Large-scale clusters, serving systems, networks, and operational designs built primarily for frontier-model inference.

adjudication.decision: Do not require ordinary startups to build frontier inference infrastructure.
adjudication.rationale: The evidence supports inference optimization and model-path selection, but frontier clusters are a supplier capability and a conditional concern for infrastructure companies. Most startups should consume this capability through routing, capacity, latency, and cost controls rather than own the underlying cluster.

evidence_review.finding: New multi-GPU serving, networking, and decoding records strengthen the supplier-side infrastructure signal, but they still do not show that an application startup should own a frontier cluster. The reusable requirement remains routing, capacity, latency, cost control, and fallback selection across externally supplied inference paths.

candidate_pool.title: Skills, protocols & integrations
candidate_pool.description: Reusable capabilities, connectors, protocols, and application interfaces that let models and agents act beyond a chat session.

adjudication.decision: Do not create a separate requirement for skills, protocols, and integrations.
adjudication.rationale: Reusable skills and governed tool interfaces are one operating layer inside the modular agent stack. Splitting them into a second requirement would duplicate the existing obligations to version capabilities independently, constrain permissions, evaluate behavior, and preserve replaceable model and execution layers.

evidence_review.finding: Evaluated domain skills, repeatable deployment skills, MCP authorization, and graph-structured skill optimization materially strengthen technical reality. Direct API and single-agent critiques remain valid counterevidence: an interoperability layer is useful when governance or reuse warrants it, not as mandatory ceremony for every simple workflow.

candidate_pool.title: Training, evaluation & self-improvement
candidate_pool.description: Methods and systems that improve model or agent performance through training, feedback, evaluation, optimization, or generated experience.

adjudication.decision: Merge the operating conclusion into evaluation and release gates; do not require every startup to train or self-improve models.
adjudication.rationale: Training, feedback, evaluation, and self-improvement describe a wide capability family. The general startup obligation is narrower: measure representative workflow behavior and prevent unverified outputs or system changes from crossing a consequential boundary. Model training and recursive improvement remain optional strategies for teams whose economics and product require them.

evidence_review.finding: Payment authorization, calibrated abstention, and replay-gated procedural memory show evaluation operating inside action and improvement loops. They strengthen technical reality for evaluation gates, but the corpus remains paper-heavy and does not establish repeatable production adoption or make model training a universal startup requirement.

candidate_pool.title: Heterogeneous model portfolios are becoming the default inference architecture
candidate_pool.description: Teams will combine frontier, small, open, local, and specialized models through routing and purpose-built serving rather than standardizing on one endpoint.

candidate_pool.title: Validation is becoming the release gate for AI-generated work
candidate_pool.description: As agents produce code and operational changes, evaluation, observability, security, and reversible deployment become one continuous release discipline.

candidate_pool.title: Agent harnesses
candidate_pool.description: Control systems around models that manage planning, tools, state, execution, recovery, and multi-agent coordination.

adjudication.decision: Do not create a duplicate requirement.
adjudication.rationale: An agent harness is the orchestration and control portion of the already-calibrated modular agent operating stack. Its evidence should strengthen that requirement rather than create a second entry with an indistinguishable operating prescription.

evidence_review.finding: Component-level harness experiments strengthen technical reality, but an industrial comparison found a single-agent baseline faster and cheaper without a consistent quality loss. The linked requirement remains emerging and explicitly conditional.

candidate_pool.title: The agent stack is separating into modular operating layers
candidate_pool.description: Models are becoming replaceable components inside a larger system of harnesses, reusable skills, execution environments, and assurance controls.

adjudication.decision: Keep one calibrated modular-stack requirement; do not duplicate the Early Signal direction.
adjudication.rationale: Early Signal lifecycle measures attention, breadth, and persistence, while Operating Model maturity requires technical and operational proof. The direction can be established as an industry signal while the corresponding startup requirement remains emerging because independent production adoption is still only moderate.

evidence_review.finding: The direction and requirement refer to the same architecture. Additional signal breadth does not overcome the requirement's explicit blockers: strong operational adoption and strong evidence independence.

candidate_pool.title: Robotics & embodied AI
candidate_pool.description: Models, datasets, simulations, and control systems that connect learned intelligence to physical sensing and action.

adjudication.decision: Add a conditional requirement for physical-AI startups, not a universal startup requirement.
adjudication.rationale: Robotics activity is broad enough to deserve an operating conclusion, but the actionable requirement is narrower than the theme: physical-AI teams should use simulation, staged real-world validation, and explicit sim-to-real checks before scaling autonomous deployment.

candidate_pool.title: Assurance infrastructure
candidate_pool.description: Evaluation, security, observability, permissions, governance, and provenance required to operate AI systems safely.

candidate_pool.title: Documents, retrieval & knowledge systems
candidate_pool.description: Parsing, retrieval, structured generation, graphs, and data systems that make private or complex information usable by AI workflows.

candidate_pool.title: Memory & context engineering
candidate_pool.description: Techniques for selecting, compressing, persisting, and retrieving context across long-running model or agent activity.

candidate_pool.title: Multimodal generation & 3D
candidate_pool.description: Systems that generate, edit, understand, or reconstruct images, video, spatial scenes, avatars, and three-dimensional environments.

adjudication.decision: Treat multimodal generation and 3D as a capability domain, not a general startup operating requirement.
adjudication.rationale: Images, video, spatial interfaces, and 3D generation can define the product for design, media, robotics, commerce, or simulation companies. They do not create one reusable operating obligation for startups outside those domains. Teams that adopt the modality still inherit the existing requirements for evaluation, bounded actions, provenance, and workflow-specific release criteria.

evidence_review.finding: Ten source families and twenty-seven technical records establish broad capability progress, but the evidence spans unrelated product domains and benchmarks. It does not establish a common operating practice, measurable cost of absence, or production control that every AI startup should implement.

candidate_pool.title: Enterprise context is evolving from document retrieval into an operational ontology
candidate_pool.description: Agents need governed business objects, relationships, permissions, and actions—not only retrieved text—to operate reliably inside companies.

candidate_pool.title: Evaluation is moving from a final benchmark into the system-design loop
candidate_pool.description: 12 classified posts across 5 experts discuss evaluation, training feedback, or self-improvement. The shared engineering direction is toward measuring behavior continuously while the system is being built, rather than treating one benchmark score as a release verdict.

adjudication.decision: Use the expert pattern as directional context for evaluation and release gates, not as a separate requirement.
adjudication.rationale: The expert synthesis correctly describes a shift from one final benchmark toward continuous, task-specific evaluation. That is the engineering rationale already encoded by evaluation and release gates. Creating another requirement would duplicate the same practice while promoting social interpretation beyond its evidentiary role.

evidence_review.finding: Five experts provide independent narrative breadth, but social observations do not verify deployment or effectiveness. The finding is retained as directional context; technical support comes from the calibrated benchmark, authorization, abstention, and regression-testing records linked to the existing requirement.

candidate_pool.title: Enterprise & vertical AI
candidate_pool.description: AI products adapted to industry workflows, governed organizational data, and live business systems.

candidate_pool.title: Operational ontology
candidate_pool.description: A governed semantic layer connecting business objects, relationships, rules, and actions for people and agents.

candidate_pool.title: Task-shaped models are becoming an engineering alternative to universal-model calls
candidate_pool.description: 13 posts across 2 experts point toward small, open, local, or routed models selected for a specific decision. The emerging idea is to spend frontier-model reasoning only where the workflow actually requires it.

candidate_pool.title: Simulation is becoming the development environment for physical AI
candidate_pool.description: World models, synthetic environments, and evaluation loops will mature before broadly deployed autonomous physical systems.

candidate_pool.title: Attention is shifting from agent demos to the operating layer around them
candidate_pool.description: 8 posts across 4 experts connect harness behavior, coding agents, or assurance. The common concern is not simply whether a model can act, but how its context, tools, permissions, and failure recovery are engineered.

candidate_pool.title: Specialized inference silicon
candidate_pool.description: Chips and computer architectures designed specifically to reduce the latency, energy, or cost of model inference.

candidate_pool.title: Model routing & heterogeneous stacks
candidate_pool.description: Systems that select or combine models according to task, cost, latency, capability, privacy, or reliability requirements.

candidate_pool.title: AI products are moving from assistance toward bounded workflow ownership
candidate_pool.description: The important product boundary is shifting from generating an answer to carrying a well-defined task from trigger to verified outcome.

candidate_pool.title: The commercial narrative has moved from copilots to workflow ownership
candidate_pool.description: 15 essays across 2 publishers describe AI as a workforce, teammate, revenue engine, system of action, autopilot, or employee. The shared product thesis is not a better interface for a human task; it is a bounded system that carries the task from trigger to outcome.

candidate_pool.title: Validation & release infrastructure
candidate_pool.description: Testing, review, runtime validation, and deployment controls that determine whether AI-generated work is safe to release.

candidate_pool.title: Web & browser automation
candidate_pool.description: Agent capabilities for navigating websites, collecting permitted web data, operating forms, and executing browser-based workflows.

candidate_pool.title: AI-native GTM is a named category, but not yet a cross-source conclusion
candidate_pool.description: 2 essays from 1 publisher describe an AI revenue engine and a system of action for organic growth. The interesting abstraction is a closed loop from market signal to executed action, but independent narrative confirmation is absent in this corpus.

candidate_pool.title: AI-native GTM
candidate_pool.description: AI systems that execute or coordinate prospecting, sales, marketing, customer intelligence, and revenue operations.

candidate_pool.title: Assurance is becoming a separate infrastructure layer for agents
candidate_pool.description: 7 essays across 3 publishers converge on runtime controls: vulnerability discovery, penetration testing, identity, data sovereignty, defensive models, and detection of abnormal agent intent. In the wider radar this theme appears across 16 sources and 222 support units.

candidate_pool.title: The coding-agent opportunity is shifting below the assistant interface
candidate_pool.description: 4 essays across 3 publishers focus on the environment around the agent: a full-stack cloud, software implementation, production operations, and scientific judgment. The broader coding-agent theme scores 85.2 and appears across 15 radar sources.

candidate_pool.title: Inference is being productized as a control plane, not a commodity endpoint
candidate_pool.description: 3 essays across 2 publishers frame specialized runtimes, inference clusters, and model routing as products in their own right. The common bet is that cost, latency, model selection, and workload fit will require active control rather than a single default provider.

candidate_pool.title: Physical AI is being organized around world models and simulation before deployment
candidate_pool.description: 5 essays across 2 publishers connect spatial world models, robotics, and high-fidelity simulation. The recurring idea is that embodied systems need safe, scalable environments in which to learn, test, and validate before acting in the physical world.
